analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Feedback Power 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Desk sees little urgency to play offense in the power complex. Higher-beta names (BTM, fuel cells, nuclear) are coming up less in conversations than earlier in the fall.
Dedicated investors are asking for low beta, high quality, fortress balance sheet, low capital requirement ways to play power.
The desk does not think the power trade has lost all of its steam. Specialists are still focused on certain subsectors, with some describing a 'shoot first then aim' response to price action.
IPPs: the common view is to avoid ERCOT exposure and, if owning the group, hold PJM exposure or names with positive momentum on contracting. A short on the group is hard to press at current levels.
IPP holders are frustrated because installed capacity in the ground is seen as worth more now than a few months or weeks ago. Batch Zero updates in ERCOT are due December 10 and 17.
Regulated utilities are no longer trading as a bond proxy, with the 10Y peaking in early October. Investors are discussing stock-specific ideas again.
Within regulated utilities, dedicated investors see less reason to lean into TX/OH/GA/IL exposed names and are increasingly willing to own LA/Carolinas/MO.

BTM: the euphoria seen in September has largely dissipated and investors are moving past 'doomsday scenario' framing (full credit for capex, zero multiple on power). Those still focused on the theme prefer contracts already signed or with high confidence of execution before year-end.

Midstream has drawn capital over the last year-plus as a low beta way to play power and gas volume growth. Current questions are whether stocks re-rate meaningfully or just trade back to the top of historical bands.
Generalists are focused on WMB in midstream. Specialists are focused on WMB and DTM.

GS Prime Desk (Vincent Lin): exposure to medium-term momentum is on track to fall for a sixth straight month to its lowest level since Dec 2022 (20th percentile over 5 years), while exposure to value has risen sharply to 5-year highs.
